provider: Florida Department of Education, Office of Student Financial Assistance
name: Florida Bright Futures: Florida Academic Scholars (FAS)
value: Covers 100% of tuition and applicable fees at a Florida public institution (comparable fixed amount at eligible private institutions); summer terms can be covered. Top FAS scholars in each district receive an additional per credit hour award.
deadline: Submit the Florida Financial Aid Application (FFAA) between October 1, 2026 and August 31, 2027 (2027 graduates). Tests must be taken on or before August 31 of the graduation year.
apply: Florida Financial Aid Application (FFAA); eligibility is evaluated from high school transcript and test data
eligibility: Florida resident and U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen; standard Florida high school diploma; 16 college-preparatory courses; 3.50 weighted Bright Futures GPA in those courses; for 2026-27 graduates ACT 29, CLT 95, or SAT 1330; 100 volunteer service hours, 100 paid work hours, or 100 combined hours. National Merit Finalists/Scholars, AP Capstone, AICE Diploma and IB Diploma recipients have alternate qualifying paths. Must enroll at an eligible Florida institution.
notes: Only usable at eligible Florida colleges. Renewal requires a 3.0 unweighted college GPA. Requirements can change each legislative session.

provider: Florida Department of Education, Office of Student Financial Assistance
name: Florida Bright Futures: Florida Medallion Scholars (FMS)
value: Covers 75% of tuition and applicable fees at a Florida public institution (100% for associate degree programs at Florida College System institutions); comparable fixed amount at eligible private institutions.
deadline: Submit the Florida Financial Aid Application (FFAA) between October 1, 2026 and August 31, 2027 (2027 graduates).
apply: Florida Financial Aid Application (FFAA)
eligibility: Florida resident and U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen; standard Florida high school diploma; 16 college-preparatory courses; 3.00 weighted Bright Futures GPA; for 2026-27 graduates ACT 24, CLT 82, or SAT 1190; 75 volunteer service hours, 100 paid work hours, or 100 combined hours. Must enroll at an eligible Florida institution.
notes: Only usable at eligible Florida colleges. Renewal requires a 2.75 unweighted college GPA.

name: HOPE Scholarship
value: Award applied toward standard undergraduate tuition at eligible Georgia public colleges (up to 15 hours) or a set amount at eligible private colleges (up to 12 hours). See GSFC award amount tables.
deadline: Application deadline is the last day of the school term or the student's withdrawal date, whichever occurs first. Apply as early as possible.
apply: Complete the FAFSA or the Georgia Student Finance Application (GSFAPP); HOPE GPA is calculated from transcript data your Georgia high school submits
eligibility: Georgia resident; U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen; graduate from an eligible high school with a minimum 3.0 calculated HOPE GPA and at least four full rigor credits from the Academic Rigor Course List; enroll as a degree-seeking student at a HOPE-eligible college in Georgia.
notes: Only usable at HOPE-eligible colleges in Georgia. Out-of-state and some home study graduates are evaluated manually.

name: Zell Miller Scholarship
value: Award applied toward standard undergraduate tuition at eligible Georgia public colleges (up to 15 hours) or a set amount at eligible private colleges (up to 12 hours). See GSFC award amount tables.
deadline: Application deadline is the last day of the school term or the student's withdrawal date, whichever occurs first.
apply: Complete the FAFSA or the Georgia Student Finance Application (GSFAPP)
eligibility: Georgia resident; U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen; graduate from an eligible high school with a minimum 3.7 calculated HOPE GPA, at least four full rigor credits, and a minimum 1200 SAT or 25 ACT on a single test administration before graduation. Alternatively, the named Zell Miller valedictorian or salutatorian with a minimum 3.0 HOPE GPA and four rigor credits qualifies.
notes: Only usable at eligible Georgia colleges. Students not eligible at high school graduation cannot gain Zell Miller eligibility in college. The 3.0 valedictorian/salutatorian path is an exception to the 3.7 minimum.

provider: Tennessee Higher Education Commission and Student Assistance Corporation
name: Tennessee HOPE Scholarship
value: Four-year institutions (and two-year institutions with on-campus housing): up to $2,250 per full-time semester as a freshman and sophomore, then up to $2,850 per full-time semester as a junior and senior. Two-year institutions: up to $1,600 per full-time semester.
deadline: FAFSA deadlines: 09/01 for fall, 03/01 for spring, 05/01 for summer (displayed without a year)
apply: Complete the FAFSA
eligibility: Tennessee resident who graduates from an eligible Tennessee high school and earns a minimum 21 ACT or 1060 SAT, OR an overall minimum 3.0 GPA (4.0 scale with additional points for AP, honors and similar courses under the Uniform Grading Policy). Must enroll at an eligible postsecondary institution within 16 months of graduation.
notes: Used at eligible Tennessee public and private colleges. ACT superscores and residual tests are not accepted.

provider: Tennessee Higher Education Commission and Student Assistance Corporation
name: General Assembly Merit Scholarship (HOPE supplement)
value: Up to $500 per semester as a supplement to the HOPE Scholarship, including summer.
deadline: FAFSA must be received by September 1st for fall, March 1st for spring and May 1st for summer (displayed without a year)
apply: Complete the FAFSA (applies for both HOPE and the GAMS supplement)
eligibility: Graduates of a Tennessee public school or category 1, 2 or 3 private school with a minimum 3.75 GPA (4.0 scale with additional points for AP, honors and similar courses) AND a 29 ACT or 1330 SAT, taken on a national or state test date before college enrollment. Must also be HOPE eligible.
notes: Only usable at eligible Tennessee institutions. ACT superscores are not accepted.

provider: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
name: Palmetto Fellows Scholarship
value: Up to $6,700 freshman year and up to $7,500 each for sophomore, junior and senior years, applied to cost of attendance. Fellows in approved math, science, education or accounting majors can receive up to $10,000 per year combined with the Scholarship Enhancement starting sophomore year.
deadline: Early Awards: April 15; Late Awards: June 30 of the senior year (displayed without a year)
apply: Application is initiated by the school counselor; eligible students receive an electronic application link and submit it themselves
eligibility: South Carolina resident; U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident. Early Awards: 1200 SAT or 25 ACT by the March test, 3.50 GPA on the SC Uniform Grading Policy at the end of junior year, and top 6% class rank in 10th, 11th or 12th grade. Alternative criteria without rank: 4.0 SC UGP GPA and 1400 SAT or 31 ACT. Must attend an eligible four-year institution in South Carolina.
notes: Only usable at eligible South Carolina four-year institutions. Academic criteria are from the CHE state scholarship flyer; confirm current criteria with your school counselor.

provider: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
name: LIFE Scholarship
value: At four-year institutions, up to $5,000 per year (up to $4,700 plus a $300 book allowance per the CHE LIFE FAQ); up to eight terms. STEM, education and accounting majors may add a LIFE Scholarship Enhancement of up to $2,500.
deadline: No application; eligibility is determined by the college
apply: Automatic; the college financial aid office determines eligibility and notifies students
eligibility: South Carolina resident; U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident. For four-year institutions, meet 2 of 3: 3.0 SC Uniform Grading Policy GPA, 1100 SAT or 22 ACT, rank in top 30% of graduating class. For two-year institutions, 3.0 SC UGP GPA.
notes: Only usable at eligible South Carolina institutions. Mid-year graduates cannot use class rank.

provider: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education
name: South Carolina HOPE Scholarship (freshman year)
value: Up to $2,800 (including a $300 book allowance) toward cost of attendance for the freshman year only.
deadline: No application; eligibility is determined by the college
apply: Automatic; the college determines eligibility from the final high school transcript
eligibility: South Carolina resident; U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident; cumulative 3.0 GPR on the SC Uniform Grading Policy at graduation; attend an eligible four-year institution; for students who do not qualify for LIFE or Palmetto Fellows.
notes: Freshman year only. Recipients who meet LIFE renewal criteria move into LIFE in their second year. Only usable at eligible South Carolina four-year institutions.

provider: Louisiana Office of Student Financial Assistance (LOSFA)
name: TOPS Opportunity, Performance and Honors Awards
value: Opportunity: TOPS Award Amount (tuition-based amount set per institution). Performance: TOPS Award Amount plus $400 annual stipend. Honors: TOPS Award Amount plus $800 annual stipend. LAICU private colleges pay a weighted average amount.
deadline: Application must be received by July 1 (or next business day) following the one-year anniversary of high school graduation; FAFSA priority deadline is February 1 of senior year (displayed without a year)
apply: FAFSA or the TOPS Online Application
eligibility: Louisiana resident; U.S. citizen or permanent resident; BESE-approved high school; 19.0 units of the TOPS Core Curriculum. Opportunity: 2.50 TOPS core GPA and ACT of at least the prior-year state average but never less than 20. Performance: 3.25 core GPA and ACT 23. Honors: 3.50 core GPA and ACT 27 (SAT equivalents accepted). Must enroll full time by the first semester after the first anniversary of graduation.
notes: Only usable at eligible Louisiana institutions. ACT superscores are not accepted. Out-of-state and home study graduates have different score requirements.

provider: Louisiana Office of Student Financial Assistance (LOSFA)
name: TOPS Excellence Award
value: Public institutions: tuition and fees or $12,000 per year, whichever is less. LAICU private institutions: tuition and fees or $8,500, whichever is less.
deadline: Application must be received by July 1 (or next business day) following the one-year anniversary of high school graduation (displayed without a year)
apply: FAFSA or the TOPS Online Application
eligibility: Louisiana resident; U.S. citizen or permanent resident; BESE-approved high school; minimum 3.50 TOPS Core Curriculum GPA; 19.0 TOPS core units; minimum ACT 31 (34 for Louisiana residents graduating from an eligible out-of-state high school). Enroll full time as a first-time freshman.
notes: Added by Act 347 of 2025, starting with 2024-25 graduates. Only usable at eligible Louisiana institutions. ACT superscores are not accepted.

name: Kentucky Educational Excellence Scholarship (KEES)
value: Earned each high school year by GPA: $187 (2.75) up to $500 (4.0) per year of high school. ACT/SAT bonus up to $500 (ACT 28+ or SAT 1300+). Students eligible for free or reduced-price lunch can add AP, IB or Cambridge exam bonuses of $200 to $300 per qualifying exam.
deadline: No application
apply: None; awards are based on grades and scores reported by the high school
eligibility: Kentucky resident and U.S. citizen at a certified high school who earns at least a 2.75 GPA in a high school year (minimum raised to 2.75 beginning 2026-27) in an approved curriculum and plans to attend a participating college. Not a convicted felon.
notes: Usable at participating Kentucky colleges; out-of-state use only through the Academic Common Market for programs not offered in Kentucky. Renewal requires a 2.5 college GPA after year one, then 3.0 for the full award.

name: Governor Guinn Millennium Scholarship
value: Up to $10,000 in tuition, paid per credit hour up to 15 credits a semester: $40 lower division / $60 upper division at NSHE community colleges, $60 at Nevada State University, $80 at all other eligible institutions.
deadline: No application for traditional Nevada high school graduates; eligible students are notified by mail in July or August after graduation
apply: Automatic for graduates of Nevada public, private or charter high schools (school reports eligible names); home schooled and out-of-state high school students must apply
eligibility: Graduate from a Nevada high school with an overall 3.25 GPA (weighted or unweighted) OR an SAT 1070+ or ACT 21+; complete 4 years English, 4 years math (including Algebra II or higher), 3 years science and 3 years history; Nevada resident for at least two years.
notes: Only usable at eligible in-state Nevada institutions.

provider: West Virginia Higher Education Policy Commission
name: PROMISE Scholarship
value: $5,500 per year or the cost of tuition and mandatory fees, whichever is less, at eligible West Virginia public or independent institutions.
deadline: Class of 2027: complete the Promise Scholarship application and FAFSA by March 1, 2027
apply: Promise Scholarship application (via WVSAM) plus the FAFSA
eligibility: West Virginia residency for 12 consecutive months before the deadline; complete graduation requirements at a West Virginia high school; overall GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale; ACT composite 21 or SAT 1080 by the July ACT or June SAT test date (superscores accepted for 2027-28); U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen.
notes: Only usable at eligible West Virginia institutions. Late applicants may only be considered for a spring award if funds remain.

provider: Mississippi Office of Student Financial Aid
name: Mississippi Eminent Scholars Grant (MESG)
value: Up to $2,500 per academic year, not to exceed tuition and required fees; up to 8 semesters.
deadline: Application dates: October 1 to September 15; supporting documents due October 15 (displayed without a year)
apply: Mississippi Aid Application (MAAPP), completed each year, plus residency documents
eligibility: Legal resident of Mississippi for one year before high school completion; high school cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale; ACT 29 (SAT 1330) or National Merit Finalist or Semifinalist (ACT superscores accepted); enroll full time at an approved Mississippi institution.
notes: Only usable at approved Mississippi colleges. A student cannot receive more than one state undergraduate grant in the same term.

provider: Mississippi Office of Student Financial Aid
name: Mississippi Tuition Assistance Grant (MTAG)
value: Up to $500 per academic year for freshmen and sophomores, up to $1,000 per academic year for juniors and seniors.
deadline: Application dates: October 1 to September 15; supporting documents due October 15 (displayed without a year)
apply: Mississippi Aid Application (MAAPP) plus the FAFSA
eligibility: Legal resident of Mississippi for one year; high school GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale; ACT 15 (superscores accepted); enroll full time at an approved Mississippi institution; must be eligible for less than the maximum Federal Pell Grant based on the FAFSA.
notes: Eligibility depends on FAFSA results (students eligible for the maximum Pell Grant are excluded). Only usable at approved Mississippi colleges.

name: Arkansas Academic Challenge Scholarship
value: Varies by college type and year in college; for example, at a four-year institution $2,000 in year 1, $4,000 in years 2 and 3, and $5,000 in year 4 (per the ADHE award table).
deadline: Annual deadline: July 1 (displayed without a year)
apply: Apply through the ADHE Scholarship Application Management System (SAMS) and complete the FAFSA (income is not a factor)
eligibility: Arkansas resident for at least 12 months; U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident. Traditional students qualify with one of: a Diploma of Merit; a high school GPA below 3.00 with ACT 19+, SAT 990+ or Accuplacer 246+ average; or a GPA of 3.00+ with any standardized test score on record. Must be accepted at an approved Arkansas institution and enroll full time.
notes: Only usable at approved Arkansas institutions. Renewal requires a 2.5 college GPA and 27 hours in year one, 30 hours per year after.

name: Governor's Distinguished Scholarship
value: Up to $10,000 per academic year for tuition, mandatory fees, room and board, for 4 years ($40,000 total). Can be combined with the Academic Challenge Scholarship.
deadline: Annual deadline: March 1 (displayed without a year); qualifying ACT/SAT scores must be earned by the end of February
apply: Apply through ADHE SAMS and complete the FAFSA
eligibility: Arkansas resident for 12 months; U.S. citizen or permanent resident (or student or parent with an Employment Authorization Document); graduating high school senior with an ACT composite or superscore of 32 or SAT 1410 AND a 3.5 cumulative GPA.
notes: Only usable at approved Arkansas institutions. Renewal requires a 3.25 GPA. Students who miss the score deadline may be considered for the non-distinguished Governor's Scholars award with a Diploma of Distinction.

name: New Mexico Legislative Lottery Scholarship
value: 100% of tuition at New Mexico public colleges and universities, up to seven semesters (three at community colleges). The Opportunity Scholarship can cover the first qualifying semester and course fees.
deadline: No application; awarded automatically by the college
apply: Automatic when an eligible student enrolls at a New Mexico public college
eligibility: New Mexico resident who graduated from a New Mexico high school (or earned an HSE or home school certificate) and enrolls full time (15 credits at a four-year, 12 at a community college) at a New Mexico public college within 16 months; achieve and maintain a 2.5 college GPA.
notes: Merit requirement is based on college GPA, not high school GPA. Only usable at New Mexico public institutions.

provider: Oklahoma State Regents for Higher Education
name: Oklahoma Rising Scholars Award (formerly Academic Scholars Program)
value: For entry year 2026 automatic qualifiers: $24,000 at research universities, $13,000 at regional universities, $12,500 at two-year colleges, plus a tuition waiver at Oklahoma public institutions; up to eight semesters. Institutional nominees receive $3,000 to $4,000 per year.
deadline: Not stated
apply: Automatic qualifiers complete the online application form; other students contact their college about institutional nomination
eligibility: Oklahoma students who are National Merit Scholars, National Merit Finalists, U.S. Presidential Scholars, or score at or above the 99.5 percentile on the ACT or SAT (for fall 2026: ACT 103 sum of English, Math and Reading; SAT 1560).
notes: Qualifying scores and award amounts for fall 2027 entry are not yet published; figures shown are for fall 2026. Only usable at Oklahoma colleges.

provider: Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development
name: Bright Flight (Missouri Higher Education Academic Scholarship)
value: For 2026 graduates: $3,000 estimated award for ACT 32+ (or qualifying SAT), $1,000 for ACT 30 or 31; up to 10 semesters.
deadline: No application; qualifying score must be earned by the June test date after graduation
apply: None; the state receives ACT/SAT scores and Missouri college choices from testing records (send ACT superscores with code 2379)
eligibility: Missouri resident and U.S. citizen or permanent resident with an ACT or SAT composite in the top five percent of Missouri test takers; enroll full time at a participating Missouri school in the academic year right after graduation.
notes: Qualifying scores and award amounts for 2027 graduates are announced each fall and were not yet posted. Only usable at participating Missouri schools.

provider: North Dakota Department of Public Instruction and North Dakota University System
name: North Dakota Scholarship
value: $750 per semester, up to $6,000, usable at approved North Dakota colleges, universities, professional schools and registered apprenticeship programs within six years of graduation.
deadline: Online application open from the first Monday in January through the first Friday in June (displayed without a year; the 2026 deadline was June 5, 2026)
apply: Online North Dakota Scholarship application (ND login)
eligibility: North Dakota resident at graduation with a North Dakota high school diploma. Essential Skills: 3.0 overall non-weighted GPA, pass the ND Civics Test, career education/counseling, four-year rolling plan, and four of eight additional indicators. Plus two of three: Post-Secondary Ready (ACT 24 or SAT 1180 plus two indicators such as AP, dual credit, Algebra II), Workforce Ready, Military Ready.
notes: Only usable at approved North Dakota institutions and programs.

name: South Dakota Opportunity Scholarship
value: Up to $7,500 toward college at participating South Dakota public or private universities and technical colleges.
deadline: First-time college students: Fall enrollment September 1 (preferred June 1); Spring enrollment January 1 (preferred September 1) (displayed without a year)
apply: SD Opportunity Scholarship Application in the SDBOR Scholarship Portal
eligibility: South Dakota resident within 5 years of high school graduation. Option 1: ACT composite or superscore 24 to 27, 3.0 unweighted GPA, and the Advanced Honors Endorsement / SDOS curriculum with no grade below C (class of 2027 has specific subcategory course requirements). Option 2: ACT 28 or higher with no GPA or curriculum requirement.
notes: Only usable at participating South Dakota institutions. No obligation to live or work in South Dakota after graduation.

name: Hathaway Scholarship
value: Per semester, for courses beginning on or after July 1, 2026: Honors $2,360, Performance $1,770, Opportunity $1,180, Provisional Opportunity $1,180. Up to 8 full-time semesters (Provisional: 4, must start at a Wyoming community college).
deadline: Apply at the time you apply for admission or before the semester begins; must apply and enroll within two years of graduation
apply: Apply directly to the eligible Wyoming community college (college-specific application) or the University of Wyoming (no separate application); submit transcript and scores
eligibility: Wyoming resident; U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Honors: 3.5 GPA and ACT 25; Performance: 3.0 and ACT 21; Opportunity: 2.5 and ACT 19; Provisional: 2.5 and ACT 17 (or WorkKeys 12). Must complete the Hathaway Success Curriculum for the level. AP, IB and dual/concurrent courses are weighted.
notes: Only usable at Wyoming community colleges or the University of Wyoming.

name: MUS Honor Scholarship
value: Four-year renewable tuition waiver at an eligible Montana campus (average value about $5,000 a year at a 4-year campus); does not cover mandatory or class fees. Up to 200 awarded annually.
deadline: Applications open December 1, 2026 and are due March 15, 2027
apply: Apply online at AwardMontana.mus.edu, be accepted at an eligible campus, and upload the counselor-signed certification and 7th semester transcript
eligibility: Montana resident and U.S. citizen; enrolled full time at an accredited Montana high school for at least three years including senior year; cumulative GPA of at least 3.4 at the end of 7th semester; on track for the Board of Regents Rigorous Core or an IB Diploma; take the ACT or SAT by February 2027. Recipients are selected by a composite of class rank points and ACT/SAT score.
notes: Only usable at eligible Montana University System campuses and listed community colleges. Meeting the minimums does not guarantee selection. Must be used within 9 months of graduation.

name: Alaska Performance Scholarship (APS)
value: Level 1 up to $7,000 per year, Level 2 up to $5,250, Level 3 up to $3,500; up to $28,000 total, usable for up to 8 full-time disbursements within 8 years of graduation.
deadline: Submit the FAFSA by the June 30th priority deadline for the year you plan to attend (displayed without a year)
apply: FAFSA listing an eligible Alaska institution (or the APS Alternative Application for non-Title IV schools); eligibility reported by the state education department
eligibility: Alaska resident who graduates from an Alaska high school and completes the APS rigorous curriculum. Level 1: 3.5 GPA or ACT 25 / SAT 1210 / WorkKeys 18. Level 2: 3.0 GPA or ACT 23 / SAT 1130 / WorkKeys 15. Level 3: 2.5 GPA or ACT 21 / SAT 1060 / WorkKeys 12.
notes: Only usable at participating Alaska institutions and approved programs. Award cannot exceed remaining cost of attendance after other non-loan aid, and students need at least $500 of unmet cost.

name: John and Abigail Adams Scholarship
value: Tuition credit for up to eight semesters: up to the resident tuition rate at state universities and community colleges; at UMass valued at $1,714 (Amherst, Boston), $1,417 (Dartmouth) and $1,454 (Lowell).
deadline: No application; eligible students are notified in the fall of senior year
apply: Automatic notification; complete the FAFSA (or MASFA if ineligible for FAFSA) each year
eligibility: Graduate of a Massachusetts public high school who, by end of junior year, scored in the top 25% of their district on the 10th grade MCAS ELA, Math and Science tests and scored Advanced on one test and Proficient or Advanced on the others; Massachusetts residency for at least one year; U.S. citizen, permanent resident, Title IV eligible non-citizen, or approved tuition equity status; full-time enrollment.
notes: Only usable at Massachusetts public colleges and universities. Cannot be combined with other tuition credits.

name: Valedictorian Program Tuition Waiver
value: Tuition waiver equal to 100% of tuition at any Massachusetts public higher education institution.
deadline: Contact the college financial aid office for deadlines
apply: Contact the financial aid office at the public institution you plan to attend; file the FAFSA (or MASFA)
eligibility: Designated as valedictorian by a Massachusetts public or private high school; enroll in a degree program at a Massachusetts public institution and meet its criteria; U.S. citizen, permanent resident, Title IV eligible non-citizen, or approved tuition equity status with one year of Massachusetts residency.
notes: Only usable at Massachusetts public colleges and universities; waiver covers tuition, not fees.

provider: New York State Higher Education Services Corporation (HESC)
name: NYS Scholarships for Academic Excellence
value: Scholarships of $1,500 and $500.
deadline: Check with your high school for deadline dates
apply: Students are nominated by their high school based on grades on certain Regents exams; talk to your school counselor
eligibility: Students at registered New York State high schools; legal resident of New York State for 12 continuous months (or eligible under the NYS DREAM Act); U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen; enrolled full time in an approved program at a public or private college in New York State.
notes: Only usable at New York State colleges. Selection is by school nomination.

name: Academic Excellence Scholarship
value: Up to $2,250 per year toward tuition (half state-funded, half matched by the institution), up to 8 semesters.
deadline: No application; must enroll full time by September 30 of the academic year after designation
apply: None; recipients are designated by their high school based on GPA
eligibility: Wisconsin high school seniors with the highest GPA in each public and private high school; number of awards per school is based on enrollment; enroll full time at a participating UW System, Wisconsin Technical College or independent Wisconsin institution.
notes: Only usable at participating Wisconsin institutions.

provider: New Jersey Higher Education Student Assistance Authority (HESAA)
name: NJ STARS
value: For 2026 graduates: tuition only (up to 18 credits per semester), less any State and Federal grants and scholarships, for up to five semesters at the home county college.
deadline: For 2026 graduates, FAFSA or NJ Alternative Application by September 15, 2026 for fall/spring; 2027 dates not yet published
apply: Apply to your home county college and file the FAFSA or NJ Alternative Financial Aid Application; county colleges notify eligible students
eligibility: New Jersey resident ranked in the top 15.0% of the class at the end of junior or senior year who completes a rigorous course of study; U.S. citizen, eligible non-citizen, or eligible NJ Alternative Application filer living in New Jersey 12 months before graduation; enroll full time at the home county college.
notes: The fact sheet for 2027 high school graduates was not yet posted; terms shown are for 2026 graduates. Only usable at the student's home county college in New Jersey.

name: Opportunity Scholarship
value: For the class of 2026: up to $800 per semester for up to four semesters ($3,200 total), toward tuition and general fees after other state aid.
deadline: Class of 2027 application dates not yet posted (the class of 2026 application ran January 5 to March 20, 2026)
apply: Online application plus the FAFSA
eligibility: Graduate from a Utah high school; 3.3 cumulative high school GPA; complete 3 advanced courses (one AP, IB or Concurrent Enrollment course each in math, science and language arts); complete the FAFSA. Must enroll full time at an eligible Utah institution the fall after graduation.
notes: USHE states class of 2027 dates, award amounts and any legislative updates will be posted later. Usable at listed Utah public institutions and BYU (Provo), Ensign College, WGU and Westminster University.

name: Kansas State Scholarship
value: Up to $1,000 per year ($500 per semester), based on financial need and available state funds; renewable for four undergraduate years.
deadline: July 1st (displayed without a year)
apply: Complete the Kansas Scholars Curriculum and be designated a Kansas State Scholar; then file the FAFSA and the State of Kansas Student Aid Application each year
eligibility: Kansas high school seniors graduating during 2026-27 who take the ACT by December of senior year, complete the Kansas Scholars Curriculum, and are designated Kansas State Scholars (designation uses an index of ACT composite and 7th semester GPA; roughly the top half of about 5,000 curriculum completers).
notes: Award requires financial need as measured by the FAFSA. Renewal requires a 3.0 college GPA and 12 credits per semester.

name: Roberta B. Willis Need-Merit Scholarship
value: For AY 2025-26: up to $5,250 per year at a four-year program or $4,650 at a two-year program; renewable up to six consecutive years.
deadline: Counselor-submitted application and FAFSA by February 15th (displayed without a year)
apply: High school counselor submits the application through CT Scholars; student files the FAFSA listing an eligible Connecticut college
eligibility: Connecticut high school students in the top 20 percent of their junior year class and/or with SAT 1200+ or ACT 25+; attend a four-year Connecticut public or nonprofit private college (except Wesleyan and Yale); Student Aid Index at or below 10,999.
notes: Income-based SAI cap applies. Award amounts shown are for 2025-26; 2027-28 amounts not yet published. Only usable at eligible Connecticut colleges.

name: Boettcher Scholarship
value: $20,000 per year from Boettcher for four years; partner institutions add support up to total cost of attendance (public partner model) or tuition and fees (private partner model).
deadline: Application opens September 1; deadline 5 p.m. on November 1 of your senior year (displayed without a year)
apply: Online application on the Boettcher Foundation site; semifinalists submit two recommendation letters; about 100 finalists are interviewed
eligibility: Graduating Colorado high school senior who lived in Colorado for full junior and senior years (or member of a federally recognized tribe with historical ties to Colorado); graduate from a Colorado high school; U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or lawfully present (including DACA). Selected on scholastic ability, leadership, service and character.
notes: Only usable at Colorado partner institutions. An early decision commitment to an out-of-state college makes you ineligible. Financial need is not a selection preference.

name: Terry Traditional Scholarship
value: Full ride, last dollar scholarship for up to eight semesters at a Terry-affiliated Texas public university.
deadline: Set by each affiliated university (see each university's Terry Scholarship page)
apply: Apply through a Terry-affiliated university (not the Foundation); complete the FAFSA; nominated candidates interview with a Terry panel
eligibility: Graduate of an accredited Texas high school or homeschool; U.S. citizen or permanent resident meeting Texas residency and qualifying for in-state tuition; strong grades and class rank; demonstrated financial need via the FAFSA; leadership record; admitted as a full-time entering freshman; commit to living on campus the first year.
notes: Financial need is required. Students who take a gap year are not eligible. Only usable at Terry-affiliated Texas public universities.

provider: Deseret News and KSL Broadcast Group
name: Sterling Scholar Awards
value: Awards to the top 3 in each category in each region, plus scholarships offered by participating Utah colleges (listed for 2024-25; for example, University of Utah $5,000 per year renewable for regional category winners).
deadline: Set by each high school; not posted for 2027
apply: High school nomination (one nominee per category per school), then an online portfolio with a letter of recommendation and essays; judges interview candidates
eligibility: Utah public high school seniors nominated by their school in one of 14 categories, based on scholarship, leadership and community service/citizenship.
notes: The official site lists college benefits for 2024-25 and has not posted 2026-27 details. Benefits depend on the Utah college attended.
